issue.title: replacement_inode_prevents_write fails consistently in this sandbox (inode reuse)
issue.description: native::task_status_hooks_write::tests::replacement_inode_prevents_write fails consistently (100% reproducible, not intermittent) in the bob-cli-ws10 sandbox workspace. The test's before_preflight hook deletes then recreates vault/one.md with the same bytes inside apply_plan(), expecting the preflight dev/ino identity recheck to detect the swap and fail with ReasonCode::VaultChanged. Instead apply_plan succeeds and writes the file. Likely root cause: this sandbox's temp-dir filesystem (under /home/bryan/.cache/sase/tmp/...) immediately reuses the same inode number for a delete+create in the same directory, so FileIdentity's ino comparison in task_status_hooks_write.rs sees no change and the conflict goes undetected. Discovered while implementing the task-status-hooks retry-timeout plan (sase/repos/plans/202609/task_status_hooks_retries.md) running 'just all'; unrelated to that feature. Needs investigation into whether the test should assert something filesystem-portable (e.g. force distinct inodes, or detect+skip on filesystems with fast inode reuse) or whether this points at a real robustness gap in the preflight identity check on such filesystems.

task_type_fields.why_not_flake: Confirmed via git stash on unmodified master @ 2254336: cargo test --lib native::task_status_hooks_write::tests::replacement_inode_prevents_write -- --test-threads=1 fails 100% of 5 consecutive runs, both before and after my unrelated changes. It is environment-specific (inode reuse on this sandbox's temp filesystem), not intermittent.
